items.followUp: Define the moment of a force and state what determines whether it is clockwise or anticlockwise.

rubric.why: Shows that a moment describes the turning effect of a force.
rubric.description: Defines moment as the turning effect or tendency of a force.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: Distinguishes the two moments by the direction of rotation about a pivot.
rubric.description: Explains that a clockwise or anticlockwise moment tends to turn an object in the corresponding direction about a pivot.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly describing the directional distinction.

modelAnswer: A moment is the turning effect of a force about a pivot.
A clockwise moment tends to turn an object clockwise about the pivot; an anticlockwise moment tends to turn it anticlockwise.

items.followUp: Define the force of gravitation and give two examples of gravitational attraction.

rubric.why: Identifies gravitation as an attractive force between masses.
rubric.description: Defines the force of gravitation as the attractive force between any two masses.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: Gives examples that illustrate gravitational attraction.
rubric.description: Gives two valid examples of gravitational attraction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two correct examples.

modelAnswer: The force of gravitation is the attractive force between any two masses.
Examples: the Earth attracts an apple, and the Earth attracts the Moon.

items.followUp: What is an ideal machine, and what is its efficiency?

rubric.why: States the ideal-system assumption that there is no energy loss, such as through friction.
rubric.description: States that an ideal system has no energy loss, for example due to friction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the no-loss condition.

rubric.why: Gives the consequence of the no-loss condition.
rubric.description: States that output work equals input work, or that the system has 100% efficiency.

modelAnswer: An ideal system is one in which there is no loss of energy, such as loss due to friction.
In an ideal system, output work equals input work and its efficiency is 100%.

items.followUp: Define torque and write its formula and SI unit.

rubric.why: Identifies torque as the turning effect of a force.
rubric.description: Defines torque as the turning effect of a force.

rubric.why: Gives the relationship between torque, force and perpendicular distance from the axis of rotation.
rubric.description: Writes torque = force × perpendicular distance from the axis of rotation.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula.

modelAnswer: Torque is the turning effect of a force about an axis of rotation.
Torque = force × perpendicular distance from the axis of rotation.

items.followUp: What is the SI unit of work, and how is one joule defined?

rubric.why: Identifies the SI unit of power.
rubric.description: Names the watt as the SI unit of power.

rubric.why: Defines one watt as one joule of work done per second.
rubric.description: States that one watt is one joule per second.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct definition.

modelAnswer: The SI unit of power is the watt (W).
One watt is the power when one joule of work is done in one second (1 W = 1 J/s).

items.followUp: Define temperature and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Gives the textbook meaning of temperature.
rubric.description: Defines temperature as the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.description: Names the kelvin (K) as the SI unit of temperature.

modelAnswer: Temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness of a body.
Its SI unit is the kelvin (K).

items.followUp: Define density and state its SI unit.

rubric.why: Defines density as mass per unit volume.
rubric.description: States that density is mass per unit volume.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct definition.

rubric.why: Identifies the SI unit of density.
rubric.description: Gives the SI unit as kilogram per cubic metre.

modelAnswer: Density is the mass per unit volume of a substance.
Its SI unit is kilogram per cubic metre (kg/m³).

items.followUp: A 4 kg block rests on a horizontal surface. If the coefficient of friction is 0.25, calculate the frictional force. Take g = 10 m/s².

rubric.why: Identifies the block's mass from the question.
rubric.description: Records the given mass as 5 kg.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the given mass.

rubric.description: Records the coefficient of friction as 0.6.

rubric.why: Uses the friction formula and the normal reaction for a horizontal surface.
rubric.description: Applies F = μR and R = mg.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula and normal reaction.

rubric.why: Substitutes the data using g = 10 m/s² and obtains the frictional force with its unit.
rubric.description: Shows the substitution and gives the answer 30 N.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correct substitution and 1 mark for the correct answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 5 kg, μ = 0.6, g = 10 m/s².
For a horizontal floor, normal reaction R = mg = 5 kg × 10 m/s² = 50 N.
Answer: The force of friction is 30 N.
